definitions.gloss: oily skin; a skin type that produces excess sebum
definitions.explanation: One of the standard skin type categories in Japanese cosmetics and dermatology. Describes skin that secretes a large amount of sebum, giving it a shiny appearance and making it prone to clogged pores and breakouts. Contrasts with {乾燥肌|かんそうはだ} ('dry skin') and {混合肌|こんごうはだ} ('combination skin').

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}は{脂性肌|しせいはだ}だ。
{脂性肌|しせいはだ}の{人|ひと}に{向|む}いた{化粧水|けしょうすい}を{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: I'm using a toner designed for people with oily skin.

examples.japanese: {脂性肌|しせいはだ}の{方|かた}は、{洗顔後|せんがんご}に{保湿|ほしつ}を{怠|おこた}らないことが{大切|たいせつ}だと{美容|びよう}{雑誌|ざっし}に{書|か}いてあった。
examples.english: A beauty magazine said that for people with oily skin, it's important not to neglect moisturizing after washing your face.

notes:
Compound of {脂性|しせい} ('oily; greasy disposition') and {肌|はだ} ('skin'). One of the five standard skin types commonly cited in Japanese beauty and skincare contexts: {普通肌|ふつうはだ} (normal), {乾燥肌|かんそうはだ} (dry), {脂性肌|しせいはだ} (oily), {混合肌|こんごうはだ} (combination), {敏感肌|びんかんはだ} (sensitive).

USAGE:
- Frequently appears in skincare product labels and reviews: {脂性肌|しせいはだ}{用|よう} ('for oily skin'), {脂性肌|しせいはだ}に{向|む}く ('suited to oily skin').
- Can describe a part of the body (especially the T-zone) or the whole face.
- Also read as あぶらしょうはだ in some dictionaries; the on-reading しせいはだ is the standard in cosmetics.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {脂性肌|しせいはだ}{用|よう}の{化粧品|けしょうひん}: cosmetics for oily skin
- {脂性肌|しせいはだ}に{向|む}く: suited to oily skin
- {脂性肌|しせいはだ}{対策|たいさく}: oily skin care measures
- {脂性肌|しせいはだ}の{悩|なや}み: concerns of those with oily skin

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {乾燥肌|かんそうはだ}: dry skin — the opposite skin type.
- {混合肌|こんごうはだ}: combination skin — oily in some areas (often the T-zone) and dry in others.
- {普通肌|ふつうはだ}: normal skin — balanced skin, neither oily nor dry.
- {敏感肌|びんかんはだ}: sensitive skin — skin that reacts easily to irritation.
- {オイリー肌|おいりーはだ}: oily skin (loanword-based variant) — common in fashion magazines and cosmetic marketing.
